overall: Los Angeles is starting the morning under a marine layer with patchy fog, keeping temperatures flat around 64-65°F with zero warming velocity as of 07:45 ET. The running max of 66.2°F reflects overnight warmth rather than any daytime heating, and the day has not yet begun its warming phase. Once fog clears (expected by ~11am per NWS), mostly sunny skies should drive a meaningful afternoon climb.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is notable — GFS (75.3°F) and HRRR (74.4°F) run notably warmer than ECMWF (70.2°F) and NBM (69.7°F), a ~5°F spread that reflects uncertainty around marine layer depth and burn-off timing. The NWS official forecast of 73°F sits in the middle of this range and aligns well with the dominant META bucket (72-73°F at 76.9%), suggesting the cooler models may be overdoing marine influence while the warmer guidance slightly underestimates it.
max_temp_prediction: The most reliable META model overwhelmingly favors the 72-73°F bucket at 76.9%, and this aligns with the NWS official high of ~73°F. For the active even-bucket market, 72-73°F leads at 46.8% with solid Tier 1 confidence and no abort signals. Key drivers are fog burn-off by mid-morning enabling afternoon solar heating, light onshore flow limiting extremes, and marine layer suppressing the upper end of the GFS/HRRR guidance. Confidence is moderately high — the main risk is the marine layer lingering longer than expected, which could pull the actual high toward 70-71°F.
